mat-6-28.label: When you’re worried about having enough
mat-6-28.emph: Consider the lilies of the field, how they grow.
mat-6-28.cta: Save this for a morning when nothing feels like enough.

scene.label: the scene
scene.body: A hillside in Galilee. Jesus sits down and talks to a crowd about what they worry about most: what to eat, what to wear. Then he points to the wildflowers in the fields.
scene.credit: Carl Bloch, The Sermon on the Mount, 1877
scene.alt: Painting: Jesus seated on a rock on a hillside, teaching a crowd of men and women gathered around him.

today.body: The flowers don’t weave or sew a thing, and still they’re clothed. Noticing that doesn’t mean ignoring your worries. It means seeing that care is already at work.
today.extra: Save this for a morning when nothing feels like enough.

pro-10-25.label: When everything feels shaky
pro-10-25.emph: but the righteous stand firm forever.
pro-10-25.hook: Storms don’t decide what’s solid. They just show it.
pro-10-25.cta: Save this for a shaky week.

scene.label: the picture
scene.body: Proverbs is a book of short sayings about everyday life. In ancient Israel, storm winds could hit without warning. Afterward, you could see what had been built to last.
scene.credit: Illustration by WithGod, made with AI
scene.alt: Illustration: a small stone house on a rocky hill after a storm, dark clouds moving away and sunlight breaking through.

today.body: A storm doesn’t decide what is solid. It only shows it. When a small choice comes up today, ask whether it could stand up to any wind.
today.extra: Save this for a shaky week.

heb-13-16.label: For a busy week
heb-13-16.emph: don’t forget to be doing good and sharing,
heb-13-16.hook: Sharing is usually the first thing to slip off the list.
heb-13-16.cta: Send this to someone who always shares.

scene.label: the picture
scene.body: In the ancient world, people brought animals and grain to the temple as offerings. The letter to the Hebrews says something surprising: doing good and sharing with others is the offering God is pleased with.
scene.alt: Illustration: a woman at the gate of a stone courtyard handing bread to an elderly neighbor.
scene.credit: Illustration by WithGod, made with AI

today.body: Sharing is usually the first thing to slip off the list on a busy day. Think of one person and send a simple message to ask how they are.
today.extra: Save this for a busy week.

rom-12-17.label: When you want to get even
rom-12-17.emph: Repay no one evil for evil.
rom-12-17.hook: Getting even feels like fairness. It rarely ends there.
rom-12-17.cta: Save this for the next time someone gets under your skin.

scene.label: the scene
scene.body: Paul wrote this to small groups of believers who met in homes across Rome. Many lived packed into crowded apartment blocks, where neighbors clashed and grudges could run for years.
scene.alt: Illustration: a small group listening as a letter is read aloud by lamplight in an ancient Roman room.
scene.credit: Illustration by WithGod, made with AI

today.body: When a hurt makes you want to pay it back, pause before you answer. Ask whether you’d be fine with everyone seeing the reply you’re about to give.
today.extra: For the next time someone gets under your skin.

pro-10-12.label: When an old hurt comes back up
pro-10-12.hook: Some arguments are really about something from years ago.
pro-10-12.cta: Send this to someone you’ve made up with.

scene.label: the picture
scene.body: The Hebrew word for “covers” is the ordinary word for covering something up, like a blanket drawn over someone asleep. Hatred keeps dragging old wrongs back into the open. Love chooses not to.
scene.alt: Illustration: by lamplight, an older woman draws a blanket over someone asleep.
scene.credit: Illustration by WithGod, made with AI

today.body: Love doesn’t pretend the wrong never happened. It just decides what to let grow. A softer reply can be the thing that keeps a friendship alive.
today.extra: Save this for a day an old hurt flares up.

pro-10-19.label: Before you hit send
pro-10-19.emph: he who restrains his lips does wisely.
pro-10-19.hook: The longer the message, the more there is to regret.
pro-10-19.cta: Send this to the group chat that needs it.

scene.label: the picture
scene.body: In a small village, everyone met at the same well every morning, so words traveled fast. Proverbs keeps praising the person who knows when to stop talking.
scene.alt: Illustration: women with clay jars talking at a village well while one listens quietly.
scene.credit: Illustration by WithGod, made with AI

today.body: Wisdom isn’t knowing the most words. It’s knowing when to stop. Before a message goes out today, read it once more and keep only what’s needed.
today.extra: Save this for the next heated group chat.

mat-5-16.label: For an ordinary workday
mat-5-16.emph: let your light shine before men,
mat-5-16.hook: Small kindness is easy to miss. It still lights a room.
mat-5-16.cta: Send this to someone whose kindness you noticed.

scene.label: the scene
scene.body: Still on the hillside in Galilee, Jesus points to something every home had: a small clay oil lamp. Nobody lights one and hides it under a basket. It goes on a stand, where it lights the whole house.
scene.alt: Illustration: a clay oil lamp on a stand lighting a family meal in a small stone house at night.
scene.credit: Illustration by WithGod, made with AI

today.body: The point isn’t to look good. It’s to let something good be seen. A hello on the way to work or honesty at the checkout can be exactly that kind of light.
today.extra: Save this for an ordinary workday.

psa-34-19.label: When the hard things keep coming
psa-34-19.emph: but the LORD delivers him out of them all.
psa-34-19.hook: Trouble piling up doesn’t mean you did something wrong.
psa-34-19.cta: Send this to someone who’s had a long run of hard days.

scene.label: the scene
scene.body: Psalm 34 is linked to a dangerous moment in David’s life, when he fled to a foreign king and had to act out of his mind to get away. He didn’t escape trouble. He got through it.
scene.alt: Illustration: a tired young man resting at the mouth of a cave, watching dawn break over the hills.
scene.credit: Illustration by WithGod, made with AI

today.body: A life close to God isn’t a life without trouble. But in this verse, help stands right beside the trouble, not somewhere after it.
today.emph: help stands right beside the trouble,
today.extra: Save this for a week that won’t let up.

isa-30-18.label: When the answer is slow
isa-30-18.emph: Blessed are all those who wait for him.
isa-30-18.hook: Waiting isn’t always a sign that nothing is happening.
isa-30-18.cta: Save this for a day the answer feels far away.

scene.label: the scene
scene.body: Judah was afraid of a powerful empire and sent messengers to Egypt for help. Through Isaiah, God says he has not turned away. He is waiting for the right moment to be kind.
scene.alt: Illustration: a watchman on an ancient city wall looking out over misty hills at dawn.
scene.credit: Illustration by WithGod, made with AI

today.body: In this verse, God waits first. That means your waiting is not wasted time. If an answer feels slow today, it doesn’t mean no one is coming.
today.emph: your waiting is not wasted time.
today.extra: Save this for a long wait.

pro-11-2.label: When you’re sure you’re right
pro-11-2.hook: The loudest person in the room is rarely the one learning.
pro-11-2.cta: Share in the comments: who taught you the most?

scene.label: the picture
scene.body: In the ancient world, a trade was learned at a master’s side, one day at a time. Proverbs says wisdom comes the same way: to whoever stays humble enough to keep learning.
scene.alt: Illustration: an old potter guiding a young apprentice’s hands at a spinning clay wheel.
scene.credit: Illustration by WithGod, made with AI

today.body: Humility isn’t thinking little of yourself. It’s staying teachable. Next time your opinion rushes to the front, ask one more question and listen to the answer.
today.extra: Save this for your next meeting.

rom-12-18.label: With someone difficult
rom-12-18.emph: as much as it is up to you,
rom-12-18.hook: Peace takes two. Your part is smaller than you think.
rom-12-18.cta: Send this to someone working on a hard relationship.

scene.label: the picture
scene.body: Paul knew that peace takes two people. So before asking for it, he adds two honest limits: “if it is possible” and “as much as it is up to you.” The other half is not yours to carry.
scene.alt: Illustration: one neighbor offering a basket of figs to another across a low stone wall.
scene.credit: Illustration by WithGod, made with AI

today.body: Some peace isn’t up to you. The part that is up to you is small and concrete. Lower the temperature of your own words before anything else.
today.emph: Lower the temperature of your own words
today.extra: Save this for a hard conversation.

psa-37-4.label: When you want what others have
psa-37-4.hook: Envy says you’re behind. This verse starts somewhere else.
psa-37-4.cta: Share in the comments: what brought you joy this week?

scene.label: the scene
scene.body: David wrote Psalm 37 late in life, after watching people who cut corners seem to get ahead. His advice isn’t to chase what they have. It’s to find joy in God first and let the rest follow.
scene.alt: Illustration: an old shepherd resting on a hillside at sunset with his sheep.
scene.credit: Illustration by WithGod, made with AI

today.body: Joy in God isn’t the price you pay to get what you want. It’s where your wants slowly get made new. When envy tugs today, let it turn you around.
today.emph: your wants slowly get made new.
today.extra: Save this for a day you feel behind.

rom-8-18.label: When today feels heavy
rom-8-18.emph: are not worthy to be compared with the glory
rom-8-18.hook: Today’s weight is real. It isn’t the whole story.
rom-8-18.cta: Send this to someone carrying a lot right now.

scene.label: the scene
scene.body: Paul wrote this to believers in Rome who knew real hardship. He doesn’t call their pain small. He says what’s coming is so much greater that the two can’t be weighed on the same scale.
scene.alt: Illustration: a lone traveler on a road through a dark valley as sunrise floods over the mountains.
scene.credit: Illustration by WithGod, made with AI

today.body: You don’t have to measure your whole future by how heavy this moment feels. Paul isn’t guessing here. He weighed it, and decided.
today.extra: Save this for a heavy day.

psa-32-8.label: When you don’t know which way to go
psa-32-8.emph: I will counsel you with my eye on you.
psa-32-8.hook: Not a map. A guide who keeps watching as you walk.
psa-32-8.cta: Save this for a decision you’re stuck on.

scene.label: the picture
scene.body: David wrote Psalm 32 after he stopped hiding a wrong he had done. The promise that follows isn’t a map handed over at the start. It’s a guide who keeps watching the whole way.
scene.alt: Illustration: a father on a riverbank watching his child cross a stream on stepping stones.
scene.credit: Illustration by WithGod, made with AI

today.body: Guidance here feels less like a map and more like someone watching each step. When a choice feels uncertain today, let that be a shelter, not a fear.
today.extra: Save this for a decision you’re stuck on.

pro-11-13.label: When someone tells you something
pro-11-13.emph: one who is of a trustworthy spirit is one who keeps a secret.
pro-11-13.hook: People only open up around someone who keeps what they hear.
pro-11-13.cta: Send this to the friend you trust most.

scene.label: the picture
scene.body: In a small town, something whispered on a rooftop at night could be all over the market by morning. Proverbs says a trustworthy person is the place where it stops.
scene.alt: Illustration: two friends talking quietly on a flat rooftop at dusk.
scene.credit: Illustration by WithGod, made with AI

today.body: Before you pass something on today, ask whether it’s news to share or a trust to keep. Being the place where a secret stops is a quiet kind of love.
today.extra: Save this for the next time you hear something juicy.
